index.subtitle: Pure Mathematician and track and field sprinter
paragraphs: Hello! I’m Kasieobi Udumaga, a high school student from British Columbia, Canada with a strong interest in pure mathematics.

My primary interests are in algebraic number theory and commutative algebra. I am particularly interested in studying the connections between these areas, including topics such as valuations, factorization, ideals, algebraic number fields, and the structure of rings. I will also explore related areas of mathematics as I develop my background and pursue research questions of my own.

This website documents my mathematical progress through research projects, expository writing, mathematical notes, and explorations of topics ranging from olympiad mathematics to graduate-level mathematics.

Outside of mathematics, I am a sprinter and enjoy track and field. I am a 12-time provincial champion in the 100m and 200m and a co-holder of the electronically timed provincial record for the U15 100m dash.
Major website updates are typically released every 4–6 weeks, though the schedule may vary depending on the time of year.

Hi! As you may have already seen on the home page, I'm Kasieobi (Kasi) Udumaga, a high school student passionate about mathematics and understanding it at a deep level. I've been interested in mathematics since I was 9 years old, although mathematics wasn't always my main interest. I originally found physics more interesting than mathematics, and it wasn't until the end of Grade 7 that my interests shifted more strongly toward mathematics. Since discovering proof-based math, I've been drawn to how simple definitions can lead to complex theories. Rather than memorizing techniques, I focus on asking why things are true.

My current interests include commutative algebra and algebraic number theory. I hope to contribute original research in these areas. For now, I spend my time reading textbooks, writing notes, solving challenging problems (sometimes), and developing the mathematical maturity and tools needed for research.

This website essentially documents that journey. It's a place where I organize notes, share expository writing, document projects, and explore ideas I find interesting. More than anything, I hope it becomes a record of my growth as a mathematician from what I'm learning now to the research I'll pursue in the future.

Outside of mathematics, I'm Kasi. I enjoy sprinting and compete in track and field, where I've learned discipline, perseverance, and consistency. I also spend a lot of time playing Geometry Dash, where I enjoy progressing through the game and grinding stars. As of writing, I have 25,344 stars. I also enjoy playing GeoGuessr, especially because it lets me explore different places, structures, landscapes, and cultures around the world. One of my favourite parts is learning the different metas and figuring out how small clues can reveal where a location is.

Beyond that, I enjoy Anime, J-pop, and K-pop. My favourite song is "Hyouriittai" by YUZU. My favourite Anime is JoJo's Bizarre Adventure. These interests are quite different from mathematics, but they are all things I enjoy spending time on outside of studying.

notes.intro:
Welcome to my collection of mathematical notes. This section is a record of my ongoing study and exploration of mathematics, covering material ranging from olympiad problem solving to undergraduate and graduate-level mathematics. The notes are intended to help me organize what I learn while developing a deeper understanding of the definitions, techniques, proofs, examples, and connections that arise throughout different areas of mathematics.

These notes are different from the more polished and self-contained material in my Expository Writing section. Some may focus on developing the theory of a subject from its foundations, while others may collect results, work through examples and proofs, or explore connections between different areas.

At the moment, this section is still under development, and I do not yet have any notes that I would consider fully complete. New notes will be added and existing ones will be expanded, revised, and refined as my understanding develops. 

The notes are organized into three broad categories: Olympiad Mathematics, Undergraduate Mathematics, and Graduate Notes.

paragraphs: I currently compete for the Prince George Track & Field Club and have represented British Columbia at provincial and national competitions (Just one legion nationals lol). Over the years, I have had the opportunity to race against many of Canada's fastest young sprinters, experiences that continue to challenge me to improve both physically and mentally.

Although mathematics and sprinting may seem unrelated, I have found that they complement each other remarkably well. Mathematics teaches logical reasoning, creativity, and patience when solving difficult problems. Sprinting develops resilience, confidence, and the ability to perform under pressure. Both require sustained dedication over many years, and both reward careful preparation far more than natural talent alone.

One of the aspects I enjoy most about sprinting is that progress is measurable. Every hundredth of a second represents months of work, and every race provides immediate feedback on what can be improved. This mindset of continuous refinement has shaped how I approach not only athletics, but also mathematics and research.

As I continue my academic journey into commutative algebra and algebraic number theory, I also hope to continue competing at a high level in track and field. Whether I am preparing for a race or working through a difficult proof, my goal remains the same: to become a little better each day.
12-time provincial champion in the 100m and 200m, and a co-holder of the electronically timed provincial record for the U15 100m dash.

expository.subtitle: Mathematical exposition, problem analysis, and experimental mathematics.
paragraphs: Expository writing is one of the most important forms of mathematical communication. Its purpose is not to present new research, but rather to explain existing mathematics in a clear, logical, and accessible way. A well-written exposition bridges the gap between technical rigor and intuition, helping readers understand not only what is true, but also why it is true and how different ideas are connected. This page is my collection of expository articles spanning several areas of mathematics. It is organized into sections covering olympiad mathematics, undergraduate topics, and graduate-level subjects, each containing notes, expository essays, problem discussions, or surveys of interesting mathematical ideas. Some articles are intended to introduce foundational concepts, while others provide detailed solutions, commentary, historical context, or connections to more advanced mathematics.
